event.detail:

The simplification is consistent with the grid-only receive contract. Suggested bucket: other (test-maintenance concern only). event.detail:
Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR
The two changed calls still require a fresh answer from the agent, despite grid rows being repeatable screen updates rather than a chronological byte stream.

## Details
Synthesis checked the fixture, encoding and caller assumptions together. fake_agent.rs:1628-1645 enables paste mode before readiness and removes paste delimiters from submitted lines; :1715 emits echo: followed by the colored submitted value. harness.rs:128-130 identifies every real TermStream as grid; :165-194 decodes styled row text, dropping color; :1131-1133 returns echo: plus text. Thus deleting the stream argument does not replace the agent's answer with PTY input echo. Grid replay/live rows may repeat or arrive from old screen content, so clearing a transcript alone is not a freshness proof. The actual callers supply that missing premise: structured_launches.rs:430-461 creates a fresh process-id/monotonic-sequence token not previously sent, retains the post-replay attachment, and checks agent liveness on both sides; restart_under_concurrency.rs:381-401 sends GENERATION-ONE-HANDOFF only after the generation-one restart and replay boundary. The fixed generation marker is not present in generation zero's input, so old replay cannot satisfy its echo. The fixture's response requires processing that line, and the generation test kills the host's child only after the response. Suggested bucket: other. Confidence: confirmed by source, no execution. proposed_drop: source-refuted regression, retaining the actual freshness preconditions rather than treating every post-ReplayComplete row as fresh output. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work consequence. possible_cover: none; no excluded coverage searched. Caveat: comments saying colored response are stale wording; the preserved echo prefix is the real discriminator. This does not certify unrelated liveness or generation-classification implementation.

event.summary: Removing the adopted-tmux-option test matches the retired startup contract
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4

## TLDR
This test required the supervisor to retain and reconfigure an old tmux server. That is deliberately no longer the startup behavior, so removing it does not conceal a violation of the new contract.

## Details
The assigned patch removes adopted_tmux_server_gets_its_options_explicitly_not_just_from_config, whose test expected focus-events and exit-empty to be set on a surviving server. SPEC_impl.md:2956-2963 says: "This release ends them at startup (below); every terminal runs in a terminal host" and "The running supervisor runs no tmux at all." The source independently matches that change: service/core.rs:6427-6439 ends the private server only with state-directory ownership and immediately calls tmux.no_server_after_startup(); :6455-6472 reloads sessions using the old-terminal cleanup result. The removed test would now test the opposite contract. Suggested bucket: other. Confidence: confirmed by source, no execution. proposed_drop: specification acceptance and source refutation of continued adoption requirement, with exact quoted text above. Could-be-highest: no; the concern considered is removal of an obsolete test, not the separately assigned startup cleanup's destructive behavior. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources searched. Caveat: this conclusion does not certify server-ending attribution/sweep implementation outside this group's patch.

event.summary: Removing the upload test's grid capability retains channel-reuse coverage
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR
The upload test still proves that an unfinished transfer excludes terminal use and that its completed channel can establish a terminal stream. Its removed capability flag is obsolete.

## Details
The only assigned change removes grid: true from ControlMsg::Attach. At this revision farhelm-proto/src/lib.rs:3777-3839 has no grid field and :3840-3844 declares every Attached channel to carry the terminal's grid stream. The receiving service/handlers.rs:1580-1618 likewise accepts no grid flag and retains channel admission before any takeover. The test's unchanged body at attachment_uploads.rs:1099-1189 asserts UploadStarted owns channel 1, rejects Attach while the upload is live, checks the uploaded bytes, retries only the correlated in-use refusal, requires Attached on that same channel, and consumes ReplayComplete. This is the intended stream contract after removing byte terminals. Suggested bucket: other (test correctness). Confidence: confirmed by source, no execution. proposed_drop: refuted by the protocol shape, receiver and retained assertions; there is no default-to-bytes path. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route from this one-field deletion. possible_cover: none; coverage records not searched. Caveat: this certifies the assigned adaptation, not the broader upload implementation.

event.summary: The upload adaptation retains channel admission and grid catch-up coverage only
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR
Removing the obsolete grid capability flag preserves the test of reusing a completed upload's channel for terminal catch-up. This test does not prove upload acknowledgments outrun a terminal backlog, or that terminal input works after reuse.

## Details
Original c3 conclusion is retained but its limits are explicit. farhelm-proto/src/lib.rs:3777-3844 has no grid capability or stream-kind field and declares Attached channels grid-only; SPEC_impl.md Grid streams:3011-3026 explicitly removes those selectors at protocol 77. service/channels.rs:120-131 allows can_begin_stream only without a terminal route or live upload; completed upload tombstones do not reserve the channel. :136-143 installs/looks up the input route independently of retained upload receipts. service/handlers.rs:1580-1618 checks that shared admission before any takeover; :1903 onward sends Attached and starts GridStream with no byte-stream alternative. attachment_uploads.rs:1099-1189 checks the unfinished upload excludes Attach, commits exactly file, then retries only the correlated already-in-use refusal until Attached on the same channel and ReplayComplete. RawPeer::next_control (harness/raw_peer.rs:76-93) discards data frames while finding controls, so these assertions establish stream setup/catch-up completion, not decoded grid content or a fresh round trip. The one-field removal introduces neither weakening relative to the prior test nor a hidden default-to-bytes path. Suggested bucket: other. Confidence: confirmed by source; no runtime execution. proposed_drop: source refutation of a regression in this assigned one-field adaptation only. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route. possible_cover: parent reports g139-l1 separately covers deleted UploadAck-versus-terminal-backlog priority testing; c3 is not cover or refutation for that finding. Caveats: no backlog is created here, no UploadAck-versus-backlog ordering is asserted, and a successful ReplayComplete does not prove live terminal input. The preceding c3 wording that called this a working stream should be read within these setup-only limits.

The first sent a, DEL, b, ESC+[A, ETX and a trailing z through the real attachment, then reconstructed the raw receiver's bytes and required [61,7f,62,1b,5b,41,03,7a]. The final acknowledgment excluded a truncated or reordered prefix. An equivalent host/grid test can retain this valid-UTF-8 control sequence; tmux quoting and arbitrary invalid-UTF-8 payload checks are obsolete. Therefore the retained finding is a specific lost raw-sequence test boundary, not a claim that no control byte is tested end to end or that the product is known broken. Suggested bucket: other (test-only maintainer coverage). Confidence: confirmed by pinned source and the explicit missing-check note; no execution. proposed_drop: false. Original consequence/caveats retained: old terminals still remain supported at this intermediate revision even though all fresh launches are hosts; raw transcript uniqueness, tmux argument escaping and recycled pane ids need different host oracles and are not demanded here. Large printable input is covered by terminal-flood.spec.ts:85-152, whose >1 MiB real receiver checks count/SHA-256 and later live input. The same helper could preserve the ready/reattach/content proof and add a fresh live probe where supported. Suggested bucket: other (test coverage only). Confidence: confirmed by pinned source/contract analysis; no product regression or execution claimed. proposed_drop: false. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work consequence. possible_cover: none; no excluded coverage records searched. event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513

## TLDR
Rechecking the deleted binary-output test did not establish a further host/grid coverage defect: viewers no longer receive arbitrary output bytes, and the applicable last-output/exit boundary has actual retained tests.

## Details
The assigned deletion removes a tmux-specific test accepting raw 0xff on its live byte stream or a reset followed by the rendered replacement character plus BINARY-MARKER after immediate exit. SPEC_impl.md Grid streams:3422-3436 says a host's output is interpreted by the supervisor and delivered as styled rows; byte-verbatim browser output and tmux's reset-recovery alternative are not that wire contract. Checked applicable output/exit oracles rather than treating correct production source as a replacement test: terminal-host/tests/host_lifecycle.rs:25-52 starts a real host and real child that exits before a viewer and asserts retained output precedes the exact exit; :590-630 checks contiguous multi-megabyte output through its last line after the child finished. hosts/terminal/tests.rs:1684-1731 and :1745-1785 exercise the supervisor runtime with a scripted host, require its final text before announcing the journaled exit, and cover the Info/record race on adoption/reconnect. service/grid_stream/tests.rs:718-768 holds a live read to prove later silent final output and exit are not lost; :914-932 requires the rendered bye row and code 5 while the stream remains open. These are actual tests across the new output boundaries, not evidence that the implementation happens to be correct. Suggested bucket: other (considered test-coverage concern). Confidence: source-confirmed contract distinction and retained tests; no runtime execution. proposed_drop: no further host/grid finding retained for the obsolete raw-byte/reset assertion or an alleged wholly untested last-output/exit boundary, on the cited contract and actual test witnesses. Could-be-highest: no established security/loss-of-work route. possible_cover: none; no prohibited coverage sources searched. Caveats: this does not certify an exact new grid replacement for every malformed-UTF-8 input case, and it does not claim that removing the old test preserves legacy-tmux integration coverage while old terminals are still supported at this intermediate revision. That historical support state remains explicit. Known c4 and l5 concern different missing input/alternate-screen oracles and are unchanged. Discovery pass 1; no new substantive defect from this check.

Reviewed commit: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513

## TLDR
At this intermediate revision old tmux terminals still run, but their test no longer checks that an already-attached viewer receives a program's final binary write or its correctly reset rendered recovery when the program immediately exits. Host-terminal tests cover a different output path, and the retained legacy recovery test bypasses the real lifecycle observer. This is lost test protection, not an observed output-loss bug.

## Details
The assigned patch removes non_utf8_terminal_output_survives_live_stream from session_lifecycle.rs (old-side :637-746 around function :651 at the exclusive base; the immediate parent carries the same test before deletion). It starts Supervisor::serve(), handshakes after the accept loop/ticker is live, creates the gated binary fixture, attaches through the real client, consumes initial replay, waits for fixture readiness and sends the stimulus. The existing attachment must then receive raw 0xff before any reset, or ESC c followed by UTF-8 replacement-character BINARY-MARKER, within bounded time/output; the serving supervisor must remain alive. The raw-versus-rendered distinction prevents a lossy live decoder from satisfying the recovery branch merely by emitting U+FFFD. No reattach is allowed to retrieve the final output.

The applicable legacy contract is explicit at this reviewed revision: SPEC_impl.md:2956-2963 says old terminals remain served while fresh terminals use hosts; :3105-3107 says "The supervisor streams raw pane output to the client"; :3128-3137 describes the raw control stream versus rendered capture-pane recovery. The changed creation policy does not make existing legacy attachment output obsolete. The retained actual test at service/connection.rs:2294-2481, pane_death_recovers_missing_final_output_after_client_resume, creates a real tmux producer but manually builds Forwarder/ActiveAttach, suppresses live output with a seam, probes pane death itself, and calls ticker::publish_pane_deaths directly twice (:2427-2433). It requires ASCII FINAL-OUTPUT after a reset and exactly one markerless recovery. That is meaningful deterministic coverage of Forwarder recovery and pause handling; it neither sends non-UTF-8 payload nor runs serve()/the actual ticker-to-publication path. Its own comment (:2288-2292) says the e2e repetition exercises the scheduling race without the seam. The removed test is that complement. A break in actual lifecycle observation/publication could therefore pass the retained direct-publication test; a lossy legacy live decode could pass the ASCII payload checks.

Pinned source searches for BINARY-MARKER, binary fixture use, non_utf8_terminal_output, non-UTF-8/byte-clean output and death recovery across Rust e2e, service and tmux source found no equivalent retained real-serving legacy test at 647f0227. tmux/stream.rs:1320-1335 still names the removed test as the diagnostic trace used for missing final notifications. codec-unit tests exercise decoding, not this lifecycle/client boundary. c6 retained real-host, host-runtime and grid final-output tests remain valid for their host pipeline and do not refute this historical legacy gap.

Whole-range attribution: exclusive base 6e423e30068b62c6cfa276c6d720ee35bb70387a contains the complete real-serve binary test at session_lifecycle.rs:637-746. The relevant path history to reviewed 647f0227 contains 47f33bbd,70bc66a9 and647f0227; the assigned deletion at647f0227 removes the still-applicable oracle. The next in-range dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4 ends old terminals at startup, followed by driver removal in1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. No change to connection.rs or tmux/stream.rs occurs between647f0227 anddbfc6975. The finding is bounded to supported legacy service before retirement, not a demand to retain a legacy test at final tip. A focused test-owned preexisting tmux fixture plus a real serving supervisor can preserve the oracle without restoring production tmux creation.

Suggested bucket: other (historical test-only coverage). Confidence: confirmed source/contract and actual retained-test comparison; no execution. proposed_drop:false for this legacy scope. c6 original host/grid source refutation and its proposed-drop basis remain valid separately. Could-be-highest:no established security or user-work-loss route from test deletion; no current output loss asserted. possible_cover: supplied g140-f4 tests deep initial replay-tail/exactly-once ordering and g140-f5 tests signal-driven no-output teardown of two legacy clients; neither has this final binary write/live-versus-rendered/no-reattach lifecycle oracle. They share the retirement sweep but protect distinct boundaries, so no same-cause cover is claimed. No excluded coverage metadata or prohibited queue material searched. No runtime tests, reproductions, live-install actions or production modifications.
